messages:
sam: Customer reported double billing when request times out and our SDK retries. Using TS SDK v0.9.2 on Node 18. Sometimes we see two POSTs for one user action. Can @jess triage?

jess: Can you paste a minimal repro and the headers you saw? Is the POST marked idempotent? If the body is a stream it may be non-rewindable => duplicates.

sam: Repro snippet (simplified):
```js
const ac = new AbortController();
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${K}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }),
  signal: ac.signal
});
```
We rely on SDK defaults (retries=3). Customer says they see duplicate charge entries.

jess: Any request ids in logs? upstream status codes?

sam: Logs: x-request-id=abc123 then abc124. Timestamps ~2512345678 then 2512345689. Upstream returned 503 for the first attempt.

support-bot: Created ticket REDW-1823 (severity=high) and linked this thread.

kai: Quick thoughts: (1) undici/fetch treats stream bodies as non-rewindable. If SDK retries automatically we must buffer or reconstruct the body. (2) TS SDK v0.9.x changed retry semantics — older releases didn't attempt to retry non-cloneable bodies.

jess: Also check AbortController reuse. Reusing the same AbortController across attempts can cancel later retries unintentionally. Each attempt needs a fresh signal or careful handoff.

sam: Customer is on undici@5.12 and Node 18.12. Is there a known undici behavior around signal/body handoff in 5.12 -> 5.14?

kai: Yes — there were changes in 5.13 around how request body streams are forwarded; 5.14 has a safer handoff and bugfixes for attempt retries. Recommend bumping to >=5.14 where feasible.

jess: Proposed mitigation: 1) short-term: ask customer to disable automatic retries for that endpoint (retries: 0) or make request idempotent on server. 2) medium-term: SDK patch to buffer JSON bodies <1MB before sending so retries are safe; for large streaming bodies, mark them as non-retriable and surface an explicit error.

sam: Can you sketch the Buffer workaround? Customer needs a quick patch.

jess: Example conversion for JSON payloads: 
```js
// ensure body is retriable by buffering
const payload = JSON.stringify({ prompt });
const body = Buffer.from(payload);
await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
```
For stream uploads it's more involved — need to either re-create the stream per attempt or avoid retries.

kai: Also add telemetry: emit a metric when SDK detects a non-retriable body and falls back to no-retry. That will help surface regressions.

jess: I'll open a PR: (A) buffer small JSON bodies automatically, (B) expose request option retryableBody: true|false, default false for streams, (C) add docs + KB. Assigning review to @kai.

sam: Customer accepted temporary workaround to set retries=0 for that endpoint. They reported no duplicates after disabling retries. :thumbsup:

kai: Follow-ups: add unit tests against undici@5.14 and integration tests simulating 503 then 200 to confirm only one charge. Also ensure AbortController per-attempt semantics.

jess: I'll add a short KB article with sample code to disable retries and the Buffer patch for JSON bodies.

sam: Thanks everyone — keeping REDW-1823 open until PR merged and customer confirms final fix.
